plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Number, Year 6 (VC2M6N09): modelling a family holiday budget, comparing options and justifying the choice in the situation
plan.shape: consolidation: the term's money skills in one comparison task, with a model of justifying a choice with more than the cost
plan.criticalFeature: compare totals for the same people and the same number of nights, then justify with more than just the cost
decisionPoints: the choice check: total for the beach trip
the hinge: how much more is the snow trip?
plan.anchor: read it, model it, solve it, check it: say what the answer means in the situation
plan.catchUp: Missed earlier sessions? Show one budget total and compare it with the money available before the launch.

studentTools: Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The fortnight's anchor on the board: read it, model it, solve it, check it
The two holiday cost tables, side by side

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. Cost a beach trip and a snow trip for a family of 4, compare them, fix a mistake and justify a choice.
resources.title: Comparing Holiday Budgets
resources.subtitle: Same people, same nights: compare the totals, then justify.

example.prompt: A cabin is $140 a night for 3 nights. Cost?

items.prompt: The Lees (2 adults, 2 children) plan 3 nights at the beach. Fill in the costs.
Use the snow trip costs: lodge $185 a night, fuel $130, food $70 a day, ski hire $35 each for 4 people, 3 nights.

parts.prompt: How much more than the beach?

items.prompt: Max says the snow trip is cheaper because the fuel is the only big cost. Find his mistake.
work: So the snow trip is only $35 more.
items.answer: He compared one cost, not the totals. Totals: beach $785, snow $1 035, so snow is $250 more.

items.prompt: The family has $900. Which trip can they afford?
items.explain: Beach $785 is under $900. Snow $1 035 is over $900.

example.prompt: Justify a choice with more than cost.
steps: Say a money reason: $115 left over at the beach.
Say a family reason: the kids love surfing.

items.prompt: The snow lodge has a 15% off deal. Does that make the snow trip affordable with $900? Show your working.
Which holiday would you choose for the Lee family? Write two sentences: one with a money reason, one with another reason.
items.answer: Look for: correct totals or difference used as evidence, and a second, non-money reason.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. More nights, a savings plan for the trip, and designing your own holiday budget, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Holiday Planner
resources.subtitle: Change the plan. Add the extras.

example.prompt: Beach for 5 nights instead of 3. What changes?
steps: Cabin and food go up: 5 nights.
Fuel and surf classes stay the same.

items.prompt: Cost the beach trip for 5 nights.
How much more does the 5-night beach trip cost than the 3-night trip?
Is the 5-night beach trip cheaper per night than the 3-night trip? Show your working.
items.answer: 3 nights: $785 / 3 = $261.67 a night. 5 nights: $1 185 / 5 = $237 a night. Yes, cheaper per night.

items.prompt: The family saves $85 a fortnight for the snow trip ($1 035). How many fortnights?
They already have $400 saved. How many fortnights now?

steps: List accommodation, travel, food and activities.
Find each cost and the total.

items.prompt: Plan a 4-night holiday for your family with a $1 200 budget. List every cost, find the total, and say whether it fits. If not, what would you change?
items.answer: Check: costs for every category, correct multiplication for nights and people, a total compared with $1 200, and a sensible change if over.

resources.label: Supported Worksheet
resources.description: For students who need more guidance: friendly numbers, one cost at a time, and a hint on every question.
resources.title: Holiday Costs: Step by Step
resources.subtitle: Nights times cost a night. Then add.

example.prompt: A cabin is $100 a night for 3 nights.

items.prompt: A tent site is $40 a night for 3 nights. Cost?
Food is $50 a day for 3 days. Cost?
Trip B costs $400. Which trip is cheaper, and by how much?

slides.notes: Session 5, the last of our budgeting week: today we compare two holiday budgets and choose.
Before you start, put boards and markers on every desk, and the two holiday tables on the board. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with probability, one last time this term.
ASK: What is the probability of blue?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 3/8
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> count all the equal parts, then the blue parts. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Blue is 3 of 8 equal parts: 3/8. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 3/5 or 1/3.
Fix: count every part for the bottom number, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Review of Week 4 probability (the request named the focus). Keep the review under 6 minutes.

slides.title: Relative frequency
prompts: Heads came up 27 times in 50 tosses. As a percentage?

beats: ASK: What is 27 heads in 50 tosses, as a percentage?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 54%
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> double top and bottom to make it out of 100. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 27 out of 50 is 54 out of 100,
so 54 percent. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 27%.
Fix: ask what the total is, and they make it out of 100.

slides.title: Expected results
prompts: Roll a dice 90 times. Expected number of 5s?

beats: ASK: How many fives would you expect in 90 rolls?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 15
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> say one sixth, then share 90 into 6 groups. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: One sixth of 90 is 15. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 540.
Fix: say one sixth of 90, and they divide.

beats: SAY: Now for our nine times table.
Write each answer as fast as you can.
ASK: What is 9 times 5?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 45
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> 10 fives is 50, take one 5 away. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 45. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 40 or 54.
Fix: 10 fives is 50, take away 5, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Times tables fluency. Keep the whole block under 5 minutes.

beats: SAY: Here's a bigger one.
ASK: What is 9 times 25?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 225
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> 10 twenty-fives is 250, take one 25 away. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 225. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 200 or 250.
Fix: 10 twenty-fives is 250, take away 25, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

beats: SAY: Now a division. How many nines make 72?
ASK: What is 72 divided by 9?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 8
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> count up in nines to 72. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 8. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 7 or 9.
Fix: check: 8 nines is 72, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to compare budgets and justify a choice.
successCriteria: I can work out the total cost of a holiday plan.
I can compare two budgets and find the difference.
I can justify a choice with a money reason and another reason.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: This fortnight we've done sales, best buys, budgets and spreadsheets.
Today we put it all together to compare two holidays.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we start,
and the second one is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 a total is reachable for everyone; SC2 comparing budgets is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 justifying is the stretch.

slides.title: Beach or snow?
slides.prompt: The Lee family can only afford one. How would you decide?

notes.answer: totals, budget, and what they enjoy
beats: POINT to each picture.
SAY: The Lee family, two adults and two children,
want a 3-night holiday: the beach or the snow.
ASK: How would you help them decide?
Tell your partner two things you'd want to know.
30 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: the total cost of each, what they can afford, what they enjoy
SAY: We'd want the totals, the money they have, and what they'd enjoy.
Today we work out the numbers, then justify a choice with more than money.
trap: choosing straight away.
Fix: ask what you'd need to know first, and they think again.
notes.prep: The launch comes after the LI: deciding needs data and reasons. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: To give reasons, with evidence, for a choice or an answer.
slides.example: I'd choose the beach: it is $250 cheaper and the kids love surfing.

beats: POINT to the word.
SAY: This word is justify. Say it with me: jus-ti-fy.
SAY: To justify is to give reasons, with evidence.
A good justification uses a number from your working, and another reason too.
ASK: Is 'because I like it' a good justification? Thumbs up or down.
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs down: no evidence
trap: thumbs up.
Fix: ask which number proves it, and they decide again.
notes.prep: Justifying is SC3 and the end of every modelling cycle.

beats: MODEL the nightly costs.
SAY: The cabin is 140 a night for 3 nights: 420.
Food is 60 a day: 180.
MODEL the per-person cost.
SAY: Surf classes are 45 for each child,
and there are 2 children: 90. Fuel is 95.
ASK: What is the total cost of the beach trip?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $785
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 420, 95, 180 and 90 make 785 dollars.
trap: using 4 people for the surf classes.
Fix: reread 'each child', and they redo it.
notes.stretch: What is the cost per person?
notes.help: Write the working for each line first.
notes.prep: Multiply by nights or people, then add. SC1.

slides.title: Compare and justify
steps: Budget $900: beach fits, snow does not.
Justify: beach saves $250 and fits the budget.

beats: MODEL the snow total.
SAY: For the snow: lodge 555, fuel 130, food 210,
ski hire 35 for 4 people, 140. Total 1 035.
MODEL comparing.
SAY: 1 035 take away 785 is 250 dollars more.
With 900 dollars, only the beach fits.
ASK: Give a justification for the beach with a money reason and another reason.
Tell your partner.
30 sec. Cue: Partner B first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: it's $250 cheaper and fits the budget; plus a family reason
REVEAL after partners have shared.
SAY: A strong justification: the beach is 250 dollars cheaper and fits the budget,
and the children can learn to surf.
trap: comparing one line, not totals.
Fix: point to the totals, and they compare again.
notes.prep: Compare totals, then justify with evidence. SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Total for the beach trip
slides.prompt: Cabin $420, fuel $95, food $180, classes $90. Point to A, B or C

options.misconception: leaves out one cost when adding

beats: SAY: Add every cost before you choose.
ASK: What is the total for the beach trip?
20 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: Which cost did A leave out?
Less -> add the four costs two at a time on the board. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's B, 785 dollars.
A left out the surf classes, and C is the snow trip.
trap: pointing to A.
Fix: tick each cost as they add it, and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point: an accurate total.

slides.title: Holiday maths
slides.pivot: write the working for each cost, then add or compare
slides.followUp: cold call one board: How do you know it's right?

items.text: Theme park: $85 an adult, $60 a child. 2 adults, 3 children.
A $960 trip for 4 people. Cost per person?

say: Let's practise some holiday maths together.
Write each answer on your board.
trap: multiplying everyone by the adult price.
Fix: reread the adult and child prices, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Say which trip you'd choose and why.
notes.help: Write the working for each line first.
notes.prep: Guided practice: nights, mixed prices, difference, per person and left over. SC2.

slides.title: How much more?
slides.label: How much more is the city trip? Which fits a $1 000 budget?

answers: $275 more; only the country trip fits

beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
Find the difference, then check the budget.
ASK: How much more is the city trip,
and which fits a 1 000 dollar budget?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $275; the country trip
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> subtract with the written method together. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 1 165 take away 890 is 275 dollars.
Only the country trip fits 1 000 dollars. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing $375.
Fix: regroup carefully in the tens column, and they redo it.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work. Anyone with $375 or the wrong trip starts on the Supported Worksheet with the teacher.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Cost, compare and justify the holidays on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: What is your money reason, and your other reason?
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: comparing single costs, not totals.
Fix: point to the totals, and they compare again.
notes.stretch: Extension: more nights, saving for the trip, and your own holiday.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: friendly numbers, one cost at a time.
notes.prep: Independent practice: a full costing, comparison, a mistake and a justified choice. The sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: Which camping plan is cheaper for the Patels, and by how much?

rows: Plan A: site $35 a night, 4 nights
Plan B: cabin $68 a night, 4 nights

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Work it out on your own board.
ASK: Which camping plan is cheaper for the Patels, and by how much?
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: A ($260) by $72 (B is $332)
RECORD who leaves out a cost or compares one line.
Their names go in your end-of-term notes.
trap: comparing only the nightly rate.
Fix: none now. Record the name for tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2: a new comparison, two costs each.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner one money skill from this fortnight you will use in real life.

notes.answer: open - listen for a skill with a real example
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can compare budgets and justify a choice?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with only the nightly rates compared matters most.
ASK: Which money skill from this fortnight will you use in real life?
20 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: a skill with a real example
notes.prep: End of the money fortnight and the term's maths units. Read the self-assessment beside the exit evidence.
